sources.note: Nothing on Boro. a full-text search for stress/accent boro|worawora|tapa over both -layout and -raw extractions: only the Westermann 1922 reference title. The article's tonal remarks (p. c. 7: 'tenses are distinguished by different tonal patterns', 'polarity tone: the change of a non-high tone on a verbal affix') describe living GTM languages in the special issue (Avatime, Tafi, Logba, Nyagbo..), not this languoid.

sources.note: No phonology content. Historical-geographical reconstruction of the GTM area; the Boro passage (p. 14): 'Just north of Buem, around Tapa and Worawora, was spoken Boro, the only extinct language of which we have a reasonable if sparse record. Seidel gives a list of a dozen words collected by Plehn, and Westermann provides names of six days of the week collected by Mischlich. sources.note: p. 50: 'Die frueher in Worawora und Tapa heimische Borosprache ist heute ganz durch das Tschi verdraengt. Nur achtzehn Woerter der Sprache sind auf uns gekommen' + the 18 words with diacritics (kelo, vrue, vrua, tata, esi, kelo, lizin, boso, aesakasu, ovo, aetaemisue, aeyina; dofo, dokoro, dokutse, dukuru, dekpa, doso) and the noun-class prefixes o-, bo-, de-, ke-. No statement on stress, accent or tone for Boro. p. 2 (general, on the collectors' notation for all five languages): 'Die Tonbezeichnungen sind ebenfalls ganz unveraendert gelassen. Man wird annehmen duerfen, dass es sich im wesent…

sources.citation: Plehn, Rudolf. 1899. Beitraege zur Voelkerkunde des Togo-Gebietes. Mittheilungen des Seminars fuer Orientalische Sprachen 2, Abt. III (Afrikanische Studien): 87 ff. (Boro at approx. pp. 100, 110-111, 114; also issued separately as a Halle dissertation 1898, archive.org bub_gb_PF0UAQAAIAAJ).
sources.note: No phonology content. Ethnographic: 'Die politisch zu Buem gehoerigen Worawora- und Tapa-Leute bildeten frueher ein Volk mit einer gemeinsamen Sprache, der Boro-Sprache, die jetzt vom Tshi voellig verschlungen ist'; the Boro word tatae 'Vater' survives as a chief's title; Plehn collected 'einige Worte' from a c. 70-year-old man; classifies Boro as '20. erloschene Stammessprache'.
sources.venue: Mittheilungen des Seminars fuer Orientalische Sprachen 2, Abt
